aboutH2: London Trauma Therapy: outpatient trauma therapy in London, Ontario
intro: London Trauma Therapy is a private outpatient psychotherapy practice in London, Ontario. It is not a residential rehab. People come in for 50-minute sessions at the office on Wellington Road in south London or the smaller office in Komoka, or they meet their therapist online from anywhere in the province. There are no beds and no medical detox.

Trauma is the main focus. The practice was founded by Jordan Thomas, MSW, who says on its website that she started it after recovering from PTSD herself. Its therapists work with childhood sexual abuse, sexual and physical violence, car accidents, attachment trauma, PTSD and complex trauma, using EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy, DBT, CBT, Internal Family Systems and somatic therapy.

pillars.title: Trauma work at a pace you can manage
pillars.body: Most people come to London Trauma Therapy because of something that happened to them: abuse in childhood, a sexual or physical assault, a car crash, years in a frightening home. The therapists use EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy, DBT, CBT, Internal Family Systems and somatic therapy, and the first appointment is spent working out which of these fits you. EMDR is available in the London office and online across Ontario.

pillars.title: When drinking or drugs are part of the picture
pillars.body: The practice treats substance use as something that usually has reasons behind it. Its therapy pages describe looking at what drives the use, building other ways to cope and getting back some control over your choices, and therapists such as Gordana Cvetkovic and Alicia Fortin list addiction among their specialties. This is weekly or fortnightly outpatient counselling, so it suits people who are safe to stay at home, or people stepping down from a residential program in London or elsewhere in Ontario.

pillars.title: First responders, families and everyone in between
pillars.body: Beyond individual adults, the team sees teens, children, couples and families, and some therapists write Voice of the Child reports for separating parents. There is a separate service for police, fire, paramedics, dispatchers, veterans and healthcare workers, covering PTSD, moral injury, burnout and substance use. The practice says many of those therapists have spouses or relatives in first responder jobs.

overview: London Trauma Therapy started as the London Centre for Trauma Therapy, a name that still shows up on its booking site and in older reviews. Today it runs two offices in Middlesex County and an online service, with more than 25 registered social workers and psychotherapists on staff. Founder Jordan Thomas, MSW, has been featured by CBC, Business London and Psychology Today, and the practice won Community Votes London awards in 2022 and 2023.

Clients do not join a set program. You are matched with a therapist, meet for 50-minute sessions, and decide together how often to come and for how long. The London office sits on Wellington Road near Highway 401 and White Oaks Mall, and the Komoka office on Glendon Drive serves Kilworth, Mount Brydges, Delaware, Strathroy and the rest of the county.

afterOverview: Keep the limits in mind. London Trauma Therapy does not prescribe medication, run group programs or offer detox, and it is not set up for crisis care. Its website points anyone in crisis to the 988 line. For people who need a structured addiction program first, it works best as the outpatient therapy that comes before or after one.

faqIntro: Answers come from the practice's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is London Trauma Therapy a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. London Trauma Therapy is an outpatient psychotherapy practice, so you book 50-minute sessions and go home afterwards. It has no beds, no overnight stays and no medical detox. Sessions happen at its offices in south London and Komoka, or online anywhere in Ontario. If you need live-in addiction treatment or supervised withdrawal, look at residential centres in Ontario first and use therapy here alongside or after that care.

faqs.q: Does London Trauma Therapy help with addiction and substance use?
faqs.a: Yes, as part of outpatient counselling. The practice lists addiction and recovery among the issues its therapists work with, and its therapy pages describe substance use work that looks at the problems underneath the drinking or drug use and builds other ways of coping. Several therapists, including Gordana Cvetkovic, name addiction as an area they support. It does not prescribe medication or run a detox or structured rehab program.

faqs.q: How much does therapy cost, and is it covered by benefits?
faqs.a: Sessions cost $150 to $180 for 50 minutes, according to the practice's fees page. OHIP does not cover them, but many workplace extended health plans and EAPs cover sessions with registered social workers and registered psychotherapists. Psychotherapist fees have HST added; social workers do not charge HST. The practice bills the Canadian Armed Forces, NIHB and Victim Services directly, and fees are paid by debit or credit at each session.

faqs.q: What kinds of trauma do the therapists treat?
faqs.a: The trauma team works with childhood sexual abuse, incest, sexual violence, physical violence, car accidents and attachment trauma, along with PTSD and complex trauma. Therapists use EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy, DBT, CBT, Internal Family Systems and somatic therapy, and the approach is chosen with you at the first appointment. There is also a dedicated service for first responders, veterans and healthcare workers.

faqs.q: Is there a waitlist, and do I need a referral?
faqs.a: There is no waitlist and you do not need a referral. The practice says it can often book same-week appointments, and sometimes same-day ones. You can book online through its Jane booking site, call 226-777-7702, or email the Client Care Team, who will suggest a therapist who suits what you need.

faqs.q: Can I try a therapist before committing?
faqs.a: Yes. You can book a free 15-minute consultation call with a therapist to see whether their style suits you, and the practice suggests trying two or three at most. It also offers a match guarantee: if your therapist turns out not to be a good fit, Client Care moves you to another one and that first session is free.

faqs.q: Where are the offices, and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The main office is at 743 Wellington Road, Unit 4, in south London, close to Highway 401, Victoria Hospital and White Oaks Mall. Park for free at the back of the building and take the stairs on the far right, next to Hakim Optical. The second office is at 9918 Glendon Drive, Unit 4, in Komoka, about 20 minutes west, with free parking out front. From Toronto, London is roughly two hours by car along the 401.

Yes. Every therapist offers online sessions, and clients anywhere in Ontario can book them. Individual video sessions run through the Jane platform, while couples and family sessions use Zoom. That makes the practice an option for people in St. Thomas, Woodstock, Strathroy or further away who cannot get to London every week.

faqs.q: Does London Trauma Therapy see children, teens, couples and families?
faqs.a: Yes. The practice offers individual therapy for adults, child and youth therapy, teen therapy, couples counselling and family therapy. Age ranges depend on the therapist; some see children from age 6 and others start at 13 or 14. A parent or guardian has to consent for anyone under 18, and some therapists also provide Voice of the Child reports during separation or custody processes.

Once you book, you get an email to set up your account and an intake form through the Jane booking system. Filling it in before the first session gives your therapist a starting point. After that, you and your therapist agree how often to meet. There is no fixed program length, and some clients space sessions out to every month or six weeks to manage the cost.
